instruments.official_title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225)
instruments.english_title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225)
instruments.current_status: Opened for signature on 5 September 2024 (Vilnius). Signatories listed on the Council of Europe's official Framework Convention page (read on 2026-10-08): Albania, Andorra, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Canada, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Japan, Liechtenstein, Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, Ukraine, United Kingdom, United States and Uruguay. The European Union is also a Party; it is recorded here as a note only and the convention is not attached to the 27 EU member states through this record. Individual signature dates, ratifications and entry into force are pending.
instruments.summary: First legally binding international treaty on AI, requiring Parties to ensure that activities across the AI lifecycle are consistent with human rights, democracy and the rule of law, with obligations on transparency, oversight, accountability, risk and impact management, and remedies. It covers public authorities and private actors acting on their behalf, and Parties choose how to address other private-sector activities.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing regional & international, responsible ai & ethics, laws & regulations.
metadata_gaps: The page blocks this project's automated link check, so link_status stays inaccessible; the signatory list was read from the page on 2026-10-08 through a separate fetch tool

instruments.official_title: Convention for the Protection of Individuals with regard to Automatic Processing of Personal Data (ETS No. 108)
instruments.english_title: Convention for the Protection of Individuals with regard to Automatic Processing of Personal Data (ETS No. 108)
instruments.current_status: Opened for signature in Strasbourg on 28 January 1981; in force 1 October 1985. Article 8 gives data subjects rights over automated processing, and the amending Protocol (CETS 223, 'Convention 108+') adds the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions. Parties are added to applies_to only when the country's own official approval, ratification or accession act is found in its gazette during a deep review (PROTOCOL §2b). Argentina: Ley 27.483 (sanctioned 6 December 2018, Boletín Oficial 2 January 2019, No. 34025, p. 4) approves the Convention and its 2001 Additional Protocol; Argentina's approval of the CETS 223 amending protocol is Ley 27.699 (recorded in the Argentina file). Türkiye: Council of Ministers ratification decision 2016/8576 (Official Gazette 17 March 2016, No. 29656), following approval Law No. 6669 (Official Gazette 18 February 2016). Norway: Lovdata treaty register TRAKTAT/1981-01-28-1 (ratification by Crown Prince Regent's resolution of 4 November 1983, instrument deposited 20 February 1984, in force 1 October 1985). Cyprus: ratification law 28(III)/2001 (Official Gazette, Annex I Part III, No. 3549, 23 November 2001). Czech Republic: MFA Communication No. 115/2001 Coll. of International Treaties (ratification deposited 9 July 2001; in force 1 November 2001). Denmark: promulgation BKI nr. 59 of 16 May 1991 (Lovtidende C, published 29 May 1991; title, number and date read from Retsinformation, full text not rendered). Estonia: Convention published with ratification in Riigi Teataja RT II 2001, 1, 3 (in force for Estonia 1 March 2002); amending protocol ratification act RT II, 03.07.2020, 1. Finland: Treaty Series SopS 36/1992 with Act 269/1992 (SopS 35/1992) (ratified 8 November 1991, deposited 2 December 1991, in force 1 April 1992). Slovakia: Ministry of Foreign Affairs notice No. 49/2001 Coll. (instrument deposited 13 September 2000; in force 1 January 2001). Poland: Convention with ratification instrument of 24 April 2002, published in Dziennik Ustaw 2003 nr 3 poz. 25 (in force for Poland 1 September 2002). Portugal: Resolução da Assembleia da República n.º 23/93 and Decreto do Presidente da República n.º 21/93 (Diário da República I-A n.º 159, 9 July 1993). Romania: Law No. 682 of 28 November 2001 ratifying the Convention (Monitorul Oficial No. 830, 21 December 2001). Other Parties (including Tunisia, which acceded in 2017, and Morocco) are pending until their own gazette acts are recorded.
instruments.summary: The first binding international treaty on data protection: Parties must protect individuals' personal data in automated processing, with principles on lawful and fair processing, data quality, special categories, data security and data-subject rights, and rules on transborder data flows. It underpins rules on automated decision-making used in AI governance, strengthened by the 2018 amending protocol (Convention 108+).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding data-protection treaty governing automated processing of personal data, the legal basis for rights over automated decisions in Parties' AI governance.

Convention 108 (ETS 108): Parties are attached one at a time from each country's own gazette act found during a deep review (PROTOCOL §2b); first recorded: Argentina (Ley 27.483, 2019).
